title_en: Parents and senior citizens can ask their children for maintenance
law: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, Section 5
rule_plain: If a parent or senior citizen cannot look after themselves from their own income or property, they can ask their children or legal heirs for a monthly allowance. The Tribunal must decide within 90 days. The allowance can be up to Rs 10,000 a month. Leaving a senior citizen alone without care can mean three months in jail, a fine up to Rs 5,000, or both.
what_you_can_do: Apply to the Maintenance Tribunal. In Tamil Nadu it is run by the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) in each sub-division.
The District Social Welfare Officer is the Maintenance Officer and can help you.
While the case goes on, the Tribunal can order your children to pay a monthly amount for now.
If you do not agree with the order, you can appeal to the Appellate Tribunal led by the District Collector.
where_to_get_help: Maintenance Tribunal (Revenue Divisional Officer), District Social Welfare Officer, Senior Citizen Helpline 14567.
